stories.notes: Spec work already completed for this story. Both openspec and speckit have been applied (status: completed) with a coordinator review verdict of needs_review. No additional spec agents should run; the story requires human review to validate ACs against actual codebase and assess cross-platform decomposition.

agentContributions.notes: Novel story — Live Preview is a new capability. Attachment point is useContent (236 callers) and its backing ContentstackContext provider. Prior run produced empty ACs; this run elaborates concrete requirements decomposed across GO/UP/MX. VCs stop at the Contentstack API boundary (mocked) and verify only observable rendered output. Cross-platform decomposition: each brand (GO Transit, UP Express, MX) may target a separate Contentstack stack; Live Preview must activate per-platform without cross-contamination.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added non-overlapping value but the pipeline executed in an inverted fashion. OpenSpec provided useful architectural context (identifying useContent with 236 callers, ContentstackContext provider, per-platform Contentstack stack isolation) but failed its primary elaboration role — it produced zero acceptance criteria for a novel story spanning three platforms (GO, UP, MX). Speckit compensated by authoring 13 ACs from scratch, but did so without reading actual file contents (useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx), basing all criteria on 'reasonable assumptions.' This means the ACs are unvalidated against real codebase interfaces and data shapes. Cross-platform complexity was not decomposed — the story may warrant splitting by platform. Human review is required to validate ACs against actual file contents and assess whether GO/UP/MX should be separate stories. Note: appliedAgents and agentContributions only record openspec; speckit's contribution is referenced in coordinatorReview but not formally tracked in the specification metadata, which is a data-integrity gap.
